name: Chris Valdez
life: “I still remember the customer who kept asking for the same unfinished story.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Chris takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I timed the conversation like a normal trim. When the bell rang we were halfway through a good story.
appearance: Chris is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a watch on a cracked leather band, Chris starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Chris always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Chris is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To offer conversation the time allowed for a haircut.
family: Orla March is Chris’s first cousin once removed. Chris gets to change the plan. Orla offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Orla says, “I iron for the young man opposite because he held my hand when the ambulance took my wife.”
connections: Percy Davila (barber customer). A free fringe buys the customer and the barber a perfectly real conversation.
